olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Find, as a function of $n$, the digit sum of $9\times 99\times 9999\times\cdots\times(10^{2^n}-1)$, where each factor has twice as many digits as the previous.
source: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad 1992

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: $A=\{a_1<a_2<\cdots<a_{11}\}$ is a set of positive integers such that for each $n\leq 1500$, some subset sums to $n$. Find the smallest possible $a_{10}$.
source: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad 1992

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Chords $AA',BB',CC'$ of a sphere meet at interior point $P$ (not coplanar). The sphere through $A,B,C,P$ is tangent to the sphere through $A',B',C',P$. Prove $AA'=BB'=CC'$.
source: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad 1992

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: $P(z)$ has degree 1992, distinct zeros, complex coefficients. Prove there exist complex $a_1,\ldots,a_{1992}$ such that $P(z)$ divides $(\cdots((z-a_1)^2-a_2)^2\cdots-a_{1991})^2-a_{1992})$.
source: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad 1992
